Let’s dive into Chapter 3: Immediate Recognition—Reinforcing Positive Behavior.
Once you’ve set clear goals, the next step is all about encouraging the actions that actually get you there. You know, it’s easy for managers—and really, for any of us—to focus on what’s broken, what needs fixing. But here’s the thing: most people do their best work when they feel noticed and appreciated.
Recognition isn’t just a nice thing to do. It’s a powerful tool—one that shapes performance and builds real confidence.
The idea behind “one-minute praisings” is simple, but it packs a punch. Feedback should be timely, specific, and above all, sincere. Instead of waiting for the annual review or some big event, great leaders are always on the lookout for moments to call out good work right when it happens.
Why? Because catching people in the act of doing something right instantly connects effort to outcome, making it way more likely they’ll do it again.
Here’s what the process looks like:
As soon as someone on your team does something well, you pause and call it out. But don’t just say, “Nice job.” Be specific about what they did and why it matters. And, maybe most important, make it personal—show them you really mean it.
Picture this: a team member handles a tough customer with patience and skill. Instead of a generic “good job,” you say, “Hey, I saw how calmly you managed that complaint. Your approach turned a frustrated customer into a happy one—and that’s exactly what we need.”
See the difference? That kind of feedback ties your praise to a real action and a real result.
Immediate recognition comes with a bunch of benefits. First, it creates a positive vibe where people actually want to do their best. When you notice good work, it spreads—others get inspired to step up, too. Second, it helps everyone see what’s expected. By highlighting the right behaviors, you’re giving your team a clear roadmap to success. And third, it builds trust and loyalty. When people know their efforts are seen and appreciated, they’re much more likely to go the extra mile.
Now, don’t get the wrong idea—this isn’t about ignoring problems or pretending everything’s perfect. It’s about balance. When you focus on what’s going well, you lay down a foundation of goodwill. That way, if you do need to address a challenge, your team is much more open to hearing it.
One thing to really remember: recognition has to be authentic. People can always tell when you’re just going through the motions. The goal isn’t to flatter—it’s to genuinely notice progress and effort, even if it’s a small win. Especially when someone’s learning something new, or stepping up in a new way, those little moments matter.
In practice, one-minute praisings are super flexible. Sometimes it’s a quick word in the hallway, a handwritten thank you note, or maybe even a shout-out in a team meeting. The key is to make it timely and meaningful.
When recognition becomes a regular part of your day, it changes everything. People start to feel seen, valued, and motivated to keep growing.
So, by making immediate recognition a habit, you’re sending a clear message: good work matters, and everyone has the potential to succeed. This simple practice lays the groundwork for higher performance, stronger relationships, and a more positive workplace.
